title: ScienceBuddy-PV: A Verifier-Governed Recursive Improvement Protocol for Panvascular Intervention Research
abstract: arXiv:2610.14523v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: ScienceBuddy-PV adapts the ScienceBuddy recursive-in-recursive design to panvascular intervention research through a structured evidence ledger, device-vessel ontology, abstention contract and retained failure bank. Recursive harness optimization and outer-loop model learning, including reinforcement learning, are specified but not executed. We audit a fixed component, rather than the complete agent system, using separate ARCADE syntax and stenosis tasks (1,000 training, 200 validation and 300 test images per task). A shared task-masked convolutional model was trained once per representation setting; its parameters and the heuristic support gate were then held fixed, with the stenosis threshold selected on validation data. On the locked test sets, syntax Dice was 0.475 (95% CI 0.459-0.490) and stenosis Dice was 0.231 (95% CI 0.214-0.249). Stenosis pixel AUROC was 0.957 and AUPRC was 0.180 at prevalence 0.00975. translated_title: ScienceBuddy-PV：一种面向泛血管介入研究的验证器治理递归改进协议
translated_abstract: ScienceBuddy-PV 通过结构化证据账本、器械-血管本体、弃权契约和保留失败库，将 ScienceBuddy 的递归中递归设计适配到泛血管介入研究中。递归工具优化和外层模型学习（包括强化学习）已有规范说明但尚未执行。我们审计的是一个固定组件，而非完整的智能体系统，使用独立的 ARCADE 语法和狭窄任务（每个任务包含 1,000 张训练图像、200 张验证图像和 300 张测试图像）。共享的任务掩码卷积模型在每个表示设置下仅训练一次；随后其参数和启发式支持门被固定，狭窄阈值在验证数据上选定。在锁定的测试集上，语法 Dice 为 0.475（95% CI 0.459-0.490），狭窄 Dice 为 0.231（95% CI 0.214-0.249）。在患病率 0.00975 下，狭窄像素 AUROC 为 0.957，AUPRC 为 0.180。支持门接受了 76.7% 的……
tldr: ScienceBuddy-PV 提出了一种由验证器治理的递归改进协议，通过结构化证据账本、器械-血管本体、弃权契约和保留失败库将 ScienceBuddy 框架适配到泛血管介入研究，并对固定组件在 ARCADE 语法与狭窄分割任务上进行了严谨的性能审计。
en_tdlr: ScienceBuddy-PV introduces a verifier-governed recursive improvement protocol that adapts the ScienceBuddy framework to panvascular intervention research via structured evidence ledgers, device-vessel ontologies, abstention contracts, and retained failure banks, with a rigorous audit of a fixed component on ARCADE syntax and stenosis segmentation tasks.
